clue.text: Leafstalk trailing river duck

indicators.note: trailing means coming along behind, so the leafstalk goes after the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
chard is a beet grown for its thick edible leafstalks

explanation.surface: A botanist describes a plant stem drooping beside a river where a duck paddles.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck of the genus Aythya, common on European lakes.

clue.text: A party opening up a temple

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A party opens up a temple to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A DO GAP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Swimmer dislodges top from sink

indicators.note: dislodges top from means the first letter of the word for sink is knocked off

parts.note: to scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately

explanation.surface: A swimmer knocks something off the top of a sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dislodges top from' takes S off SCUTTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuttle, or cuttlefish, is a sea creature that swims by jet propulsion.

clue.text: Declare sadly a tunic's been appropriated by old queen

indicators.note: appropriated by means taken into, so the queen's name holds the jumbled tunic

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain 1702-1714

indicators.note: sadly suggests the tunic has been badly treated, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares that an old queen has, alas, taken a tunic for herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' looks like mourning for the queen, but it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To annunciate is an old variant of announce, to proclaim or declare.

clue.text: Party line taken with state dish

parts.note: a do is a party
MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A political party adopts a line together with the state.
explanation.walkthrough: MA is the US abbreviation for Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolma is a Greek or Turkish dish of stuffed vine leaves.

clue.text: Self-important holy one's going after fair return

indicators.note: after places the trimmed holy word behind the reversed fair
return means the word for fair is read backwards

parts.note: a mop fair was an old English hiring fair, so mop can mean fair

indicators.note: going means leaving, so the letter for one departs from the word for holy

parts.note: holy means pious
one's here is one is; one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious cleric is leaving a funfair on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: A mop fair is a traditional English hiring fair, where servants once stood holding mops to show their trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous people are puffed up with their own importance, a plain synonym.

clue.text: God starts to create really awful, terrifyingly rich man

parts.note: Pluto is the Roman god of the underworld

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next four words

explanation.surface: A god begins to create something awful, and a rich man is terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of create, really, awful, terrifyingly. 'terrifyingly' seems to qualify 'rich' but only gives its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is one who wields power because of great wealth.

clue.text: Look out, Emin!

indicators.note: out suggests the name is put out of order, its letters jumbled

parts.note: this name supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning shout to the artist Tracey Emin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EMIN. Tracey Emin is a British artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's mien is their appearance or bearing, the look about them.

clue.text: Whipped a tycoon boxing king of 8

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the jumbled letters wrap the king
whipped suggests being beaten into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A tycoon was beaten while sparring with the king of eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped' rearranges A TYCOON, and 'boxing' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Octonary means relating to or based on the number eight, from Latin octo.

clue.text: Dodge's wings and favoured elevation

parts.note: the wings of a building or army are its sides

indicators.note: elevation means raising, so in this down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a favoured one is a pet

explanation.surface: A Dodge car has wings and a raised, favoured stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevation' turns PET into TEP under SIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to avoid or evade it.

clue.text: Talk arrogantly to others from an illusory mount?

definitions.text: Talk arrogantly to others from an illusory mount?

parts.words: Talk arrogantly to others from an illusory mount?
parts.note: the idiom for adopting a lofty, superior tone pictures climbing onto a tall imaginary steed

explanation.surface: Someone lectures others condescendingly from an imaginary saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The four-part answer spreads over 9, 12, 21 and 26 across. The 'illusory mount' is the tall horse of the idiom, which no one really rides.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to start acting self-righteously or superior, speaking down to people.

clue.text: Motion was altered drastically to cover gold

indicators.note: to cover means the rearranged letters wrap around the symbol for gold
drastically signals a thorough reshuffle of the word altered

parts.note: this word supplies the letters to be rearranged
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A debating motion was heavily amended to take in some financial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' looks like a debating motion but is Andrew Motion, Britain's Poet Laureate 1999-2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Motion held the post of Poet Laureate, so he was crowned with laurels in that honorary sense.

clue.text: Marker makes toenail red

indicators.note: makes signals that the following letters are formed into something new

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pen leaves a red mark on someone's toenail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges TOENAIL RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A delineator draws or traces outlines, so it is a thing or person that marks out shapes.

clue.text: See 9
Happy with coral being destroyed without proper backing

indicators.note: being destroyed signals the letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: this word supplies some letters to be rearranged
this word supplies the rest of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone is happy while a coral reef is being wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being destroyed' rearranges HAPPY CORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocryphal story is of doubtful authenticity, not supported by evidence.

clue.text: Pepper restricted by winter's perseverance

indicators.note: restricted by means the answer is confined within these words, hidden across their letters

explanation.surface: Pepper (perhaps a dog) is kept indoors by winter's stubborn persistence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted by' keeps the answer within wINTER'S PERSEverance.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper a speech with jokes is to scatter them through it, the same as interspersing them.

clue.text: Draw with articulated flatline textile process

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match
and means with

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so the word for flatline is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to flatline is to die, when the heart monitor trace goes flat

explanation.surface: A draw, linked with a flat ECG line, describes a textile process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' gives DYE, which sounds like DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-and-dye colours cloth by binding parts of it tightly before dyeing, producing patterns.

clue.text: Be a tourist with sense to understand

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
to see is to understand

explanation.surface: A tourist needs common sense to understand foreign places.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is to visit places of interest, which is what a tourist does.

clue.text: Go out with Anorak Joey?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: this word supplies some letters
this word supplies the rest of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone tells an anorak called Joey to go out with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GO and ANORAK. A joey is a baby kangaroo, so the question mark marks a definition by example; 'anorak' is British slang for a geek.
explanation.definitionFit: Joey is the word for a young kangaroo, so a joey is one example of the animal.

clue.text: One form of ancient hut not in tune with Sartre's philosophy?

definitions.text: not in tune with Sartre's philosophy?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: form of signals a new shape made from the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An old hut that clashes with existentialist thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges ANCIENT HUT after I. Sartre held that living in bad faith, denying one's freedom, is not authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartre's existentialism prizes authenticity, so acting falsely or in bad faith is against his philosophy.

clue.text: Peninsula of African country with no western boundary

indicators.note: in an across or down word the western end is the first letter, here removed

parts.note: Liberia is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A peninsula in an African country lacks a western border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no western boundary' removes the first letter L from LIBERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian Peninsula holds Spain and Portugal in south-west Europe.

clue.text: See 24
See 9
Refusing to change opinion of university, Wayne Slob, a mess, drops round

indicators.note: mess signals that the slob's name and the a get jumbled
drops means one letter is let fall from the jumbled pool

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A slob called Wayne, in a messy state, will not budge from his opinions at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mess' jumbles WAYNE SLOB A, and 'drops' takes the O ('round') out of that pool, leaving NSWAYABLE after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be swayed holds fast to an opinion and will not be talked round.

clue.text: Tasteless Taming of Shrew

indicators.note: taming suggests the shrew is reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: this word supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull production of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taming of' rearranges SHREW. The surface recalls Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wersh is a Scots and northern English word for food that is insipid or bland.

clue.text: Classic book author's 12-month record about the rise of a Sussex town

indicators.note: about means the record wraps around the reversed town

parts.note: an annal is the record of a single year

indicators.note: the rise of means the town is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex

explanation.surface: A classic author's yearly journal tells of a Sussex town's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Beauty, the 1877 novel about a horse, was written by her and became a classic.

clue.text: One supplying air when tennis player gets colour back

indicators.note: gets places the reversed colour after the player's name

parts.note: Serena Williams is the tennis champion

indicators.note: back means the colour word is turned round

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: When a tennis star gets her colour back, it supplies some fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, and a serenader sings or plays a song to a loved one.

clue.text: See 9
Call up the day before about ball and whip

indicators.note: about means the word for the day before goes around the other pieces

parts.note: eve is the day before an event, as in Christmas Eve
a ball is round, like the letter O
the cat o' nine tails is a whip, shortened to cat

explanation.surface: Someone telephones the day before about a ball and a party whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke or summon up a memory or spirit is to call it up.

clue.text: Case of senior overcome by auditorium

indicators.note: overcome by means the senior word is covered over by the auditorium word

parts.note: a hall is a large room for audiences
senior means older, so old

explanation.surface: An elderly person faints in a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft bag or travel case for carrying belongings.
